name: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant
description: The ChemoShield BX-2 is a subdermal augmentation system consisting of a lattice of micro-reservoir nodes implanted across the inner dermal layer, connected by a fine polymer distribution network that spans approximately 80% of total body surface area in a standard installation. Each node contains a concentrated payload of Arcturus's proprietary ChemoNeutral compound — a cocktail of broad-spectrum enzyme inhibitors, heavy metal chelating agents, and oxidative stress buffers — which is released in response to transdermal chemical penetration events detected by the network's embedded chemosensor array. The system provides meaningful protection against contact toxins, absorbed chemical agents, and low-concentration aerosol threats, and can be manually triggered to saturate the skin surface for short-duration protection against more aggressive exposure events. The BX-2 was originally developed for Arcturus Defense's CBRN specialist units operating in the contaminated industrial zones along GLMZ's southern lakeshore, but a declassified civilian variant has reached the open market with reduced automatic trigger sensitivity and a smaller reservoir capacity. Refill procedures require a licensed Arcturus service technician or compatible Helix Biosystems clinical partner, which has created a lucrative maintenance revenue stream. The implant has no interaction with standard bioscan protocols and is legal for civilian ownership above Tier 2, though full military-spec units circulate through black market channels.
enables: Resistance to contact and absorbed chemical weapon agents
Occupational protection in toxic industrial environments
CBRN zone entry without full external protective equipment
Extended operation in GLMZ contaminated lakeshore zones
social_impact: The ChemoShield BX-2 has become quietly essential for anyone operating in GLMZ's southern industrial contamination zones, where Dredge Mining Collective's legacy sites and Ouroboros Energy's older processing infrastructure have rendered the soil and air chronically hazardous — Ironclad Agrisystems has reportedly made BX-2 installation a standard onboarding requirement for all field personnel assigned to remediation contracts in those zones, absorbing the cost as an alternative to meeting stricter environmental cleanup timelines. In the upper tiers, the BX-2's protection against contact poisoning has made it a standard precaution for corporate executives and high-value fixers who operate in environments where assassination via dermal vector is a documented professional hazard, and its adoption has in turn driven an arms race toward more sophisticated delivery mechanisms that bypass the chemosensor array's detection thresholds.
story_hooks: Someone has synthesized a contact toxin specifically engineered to mimic a benign compound and evade ChemoShield detection — the first victim was found dead with a fully-charged BX-2 that never triggered

A contaminated-zone worker discovers their employer-issued BX-2 units have been filled with a diluted off-spec compound that provides about 30% of rated protection — thousands of workers have been relying on them for months
An Arcturus Defense technician who handles BX-2 refill contracts has been quietly mapping which executives and fixers have the implant — that information is now for sale

A fixer is hired to extract a scientist from a heavily contaminated industrial site, but the scientist has been inside long enough that their BX-2 reservoirs are depleted and resupply is unavailable — the clock is running
